claims.claim: The court can deal with the divorce if either party is domiciled in England or Wales.
claims.quote: (g) either of the parties to the marriage is domiciled in England and Wales. ]
claims.note: Section 5(2)(g) gives jurisdiction for divorce where either party is domiciled in England and Wales.

claims.claim: Alternatively, the court can deal with the divorce if a party has been habitually resident in England or Wales for at least 6 of the last 12 months.
claims.quote: (e) the applicant is domiciled and habitually resident in England and Wales and has resided there for at least six months immediately before the application was made;
claims.note: The six-month residence ground applies only to the applicant, who must also be domiciled there, and requires six months immediately before the application, not 6 of the last 12 months; otherwise habitual residence needs one year or applies to the respondent, both parties, or either party in a joint application.
